correctness.rationale: Each column of the signed K_{3,n} edge matrix maps two-to-one onto one of four row-pair sign patterns. Summing the signed product over two columns and three row pairs yields W=1/2(S1²+S2²+S3²-3n); Hadamard orthogonality reduces it to 2 sum t_a² - n(n+3)/2. The multinomial count times 2^n accounts for every original signing and implies rank/nullity by character diagonalization. Zeros require three squares S1²+S2²+S3²=3n. The inverse Hadamard map to integer nonnegative counts forces n odd to be 1 mod8, and n even to be 0 mod8. Conversely Legendre’s three-square theorem plus congruence sign choices and Cauchy–Schwarz nonnegativity produce counts for every permitted n; the n=8 case has the explicit witness (1,1,2). The three-square obstruction 4^a(8b+7) is cited as classical, not rediscovered. Independent complete enumeration of 2^(3n) signings for n=2,3,4 matched every predicted Walsh level; no finite enumeration proves the all-n criterion.
